chapter: Ellington band members and life on the road
title: Who joined Ellington before and after Bigard, and Elmer Snowden
summary: Harry Carney was in the band before Bigard; Hodges, Cootie, Tizol and Whetsol came after, and the Washington men pushed banjoist Elmer Snowden out and made Duke leader.

story.theme_name: Duke Ellington and his orchestra, as others knew them
story.community_name: Duke Ellington: the band, the man, his men

blocks.x: You and Harry Carney joined the band right about the same time.
No, Harry was in there before.
You joined in '27 and Harry first recorded in '27. Did he join in '26?

He joined before that, I think, because Harry was the only one -- he was so young that he went to the New England states in the summertime with Duke but he didn't play with Duke when he first came to New York because Duke was on Broadway then.
When he first came to New York he was working somewhere else.
I guess so. I don't know where he was. I didn't know him at all.

Hodges was with Chick Webb. Cootie was with Chick Webb. Cootie came after me. Hodges came after me. That's about all. But it wasn't long after. Tizol, I think, came in after me, not long. They sent for him from Washington. And Whetsql, Art Whetsql.
Had Duke known them in Washington or --
Had Duke known them in Washington or --
Yeah, they worked in the band -- they had -- a banjo player used to be the leader of the band.
And they got together and kicked him out of the band and made Duke the leader. Sure.
